cues.text: Good morning, Kenton Festival box office. How can I help you?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Oh, good morning. I’m coming to Kenton for a few days’ holiday next month, and a friend told me there’s a festival. She gave me this number to find out about it.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: That’s right, the festival begins on the 16th of May and goes on till the 19th
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Oh, that’s great. I’ll be there from the 15th till the 19th. So could you tell me the programme, please?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Well, on the first day, there’s the opening ceremony, in the town centre. People start gathering around 2 o’clock, to get a good place to see from, and the events will start at 2.45, and finish about 5.30.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: OK, thanks. I’ll make sure I get there early to get a good spot.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: The festival will be officially opened by the mayor. He’ll just speak for a few minutes, welcoming everyone to the festival. All the town councillors will be there, and of course lots of other people.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Then there’ll be a performance by a band. Most years we have a children’s choir, but this year the local army cadets offered to perform, and they’re very good.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Uhuh.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: After that, a community group from the town will perform a play they’ve written themselves, just a short one. It’s about Helen Tungate. I don’t know if you’ve heard of her?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: I certainly have. She was a scientist years ago.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: That’s right. She was born in Kenton exactly 100 years ago, so we’re celebrating her centenary.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: I’m a biologist, so I’ve always been interested in her, I didn’t realise she came from Kenton.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Yes. Well, all that will take place in the afternoon, and later, as the sun sets, there’ll be a firework display. You should go to the park to watch, as you’ll get the best view from there, and the display takes place on the opposite side of the river. It’s always one of the most popular events in the festival.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Sounds great.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: And what’s happening on the other days?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: There are several events that go on the whole time. For example, the students of the art college have produced a number of videos, all connected with relationships between children and their grandparents.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: That sounds interesting. It makes a change from children and parents, doesn’t it!
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Exactly. Because the art college is in use for classes, throughout the festival, the videos are being shown in Handsworth House.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: How do you spell the name?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: H-A-N-D-S-W-O-R-T-H. Handsworth House. It’s close to the Town Hall.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Now let me see, what else can I tell you about?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Are there any displays of ballet dancing? I’m particularly interested in that as I do it as a hobby.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: There isn’t any ballet, I’m afraid, but there’ll be a demonstration of traditional dances from all round the country.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Oh, that’d be nice. Where’s that being held?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: It’s in the market in the town centre – the outdoor one, not the covered market. And it’s on at 2 and 5 every afternoon of the festival, apart from the first day.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Lovely. I’m interested in all kinds of dancing, so I’m sure I’ll enjoy that!
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Mmm. I’m sure you will.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: And I’d really like to go to some concerts, if there are any.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Yes, there are several. Three performed by professionals, and one by local children.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: And where is it being held?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: It’s in the library, which is in Part Street. On the 18th, at 6.30 in the evening.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: I presume I’ll need tickets for that.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Yes, you can book online, or you can buy them when you arrive in Kenton, either at the festival box office, or from any shops displaying our logo in the windows.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Well, I think that’ll keep me busy for the whole of my stay in Kenton. Thank you so much for all your help.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: You’re welcome. I hope you enjoy your stay.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Thank you. Goodbye.
cues.speaker: WOMAN
